# DSH-SLOP
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that helps agents work on HPC clusters with less friction.
中文 · Install · Documentation · Port it to your harness
## The problem and the solution
AI agents are pretty good at using HPC, but I've run into a few problems when using them to manage H
s are pretty good at using HPC, but I've run into a few problems when using them to manage HPC work:
- **Access.** Clusters sit behind VPNs, passwords and 2FA. I want agents to reuse SSH connections wi

thout exposing my password to the model, and to work across HPC resources more easily.
- **Waiting.*
* Jobs can run for hours. Repeated status checks consume tokens, and it's easy to lose track of a jo
hours. Repeated status checks consume tokens, and it's easy to lose track of a job when a Chat ends.
DSH-SLOP aims to help with these problems. (Or stick with `tmux` and `claude rc` if that already wor
s to help with these problems. (Or stick with `tmux` and `claude rc` if that already works for you.)
The plugin adds four components to your existing DSH Chats. It creates no second Agent, shell or con
versation; DSH's own tools and your domain Skills still do the actual work.
| Component | What it does | Boundary |
| **Machine** | Reuses SSH logins for remote commands and file transfers; keeps approved machine fac

ts. | Protected password/2FA prompts. OpenSSH on macOS/Linux; native SSH on Windows. |
| **Knowledge
** | Markdown notes searched on demand, shared on this computer or scoped to the current Workspace.

| Digest-guarded writes; no delete tool. Disable it if you use another memory plugin. |
| **Queue**
| Tracks submitted Slurm, PBS and local jobs; notifies their Chats when status changes. | Never subm

its, cancels or retries work. |
| **Queue webhook** *(optional)* | Receives job-script callbacks so
Queue learns about starts and exits sooner. | Off by default. Requires a public HTTPS endpoint throu
gh your tunnel or proxy. |
Each component can be enabled or disabled in Plugin Manager. Queue still tracks local jobs when Mach
ine is off. How the pieces fit together is in architecture.

## Questions
**Which platforms are supported?** macOS is my main development and testing platform. Windows is exp
ected to work. Linux should work in theory, but I haven't tested it myself. See status for known lim
work. Linux should work in theory, but I haven't tested it myself. See status for known limitations.
**Where is my data?** Machine and Queue data live in `~/.dsh/slop-plugin/slop` (under `$DSH_HOME` if
set), outside the installed package, so removing the plugin keeps them. Home Knowledge defaults to
`~/.slop/knowledge`; Workspace Knowledge is `.dsh/knowledge` inside the Workspace. Nothing is synchr
onized between computers. Chats and credentials stay in DSH.
**Can I try it separately from my existing DSH setup?** Yes: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm
build && pnpm dev` starts a separate home. See standalone setup.
**Is it ready for my cluster?** Status lists what was checked and what was not.
## Port it to another harness
DSH-SLOP is built on DSH's plugin API, so this repository is a reference implementation rather than
a library. You can port the design: PROMPT.md is a brief you can give your own coding agent, such as
Claude Code, to build the same Machine, Knowledge and Queue for a different harness.
